steps.title: Declare the parameters
notes: Wall supports are on by default (FLAGS.OPT_ON), and the group has only one child: a Layer skip. Power, speed and laser come from the Scanning group, like for every vector type.

lines: // On by default. Thin support walls exposed as single lines; only a
// layer skip can be set (laser settings: grp_scanning).

steps.title: Read the values from the profile
notes: part.support_wall holds the switch and the layer skip settings, {every_nth, offset}, read by the shared read_layer_skip.

steps.title: Find the support lines of the layer
notes: Wall supports have no area: in a sliced layer they are open polylines. process_open_polylines walks over them and checks the model subtype: part paths go out as they are, support lines become wall support vectors (BSID 700).
This is why the demo shows no border and no hatch on the walls: they never reach the island code.

lines: // Tip: an iterator points to one polyline at a time;
// isValid() is false after the last one, next() moves on.
// Part paths are exposed as they are (no layer skip, no options).
// The support lines are connected and sorted for short jumps.

steps.title: Expose every n-th layer
notes: LAYER_SKIP.is_active keeps a layer if (layer index − offset) is a multiple of every_nth. With every_nth = 2 the demo exposes z = 2.01 mm and skips z = 2.04 mm, and ATU reports no BSID 700 on the skipped layer.
The exposed layer then has to melt the skipped powder layer too: the support grows in 60 µm steps instead of 30 µm. That saves time but needs enough energy per exposure.

lines: // No settings, or every_nth <= 1 (also undefined or NaN): expose every layer.
// A negative index should not happen. Exposing is the safe choice.
// Tip: % is the remainder of a division, e.g. 5 % 2 = 1.
// A remainder of 0 means the layer is one of the "every n-th" layers.
// In JavaScript the remainder has the sign of the dividend
// ((0 - 1) % 5 = -1), so it is shifted into [0, every_nth) first.

steps.title: Connect, merge and sort the lines
notes: make_wall_support_hatch tidies each polyline in three builtin calls: connect pieces whose ends are closer than 1 µm, merge collinear lines across gaps of up to 4 mm (flipping lines that point the other way), and sort the blocks for short jumps, starting near (0, 0).
Fewer blocks mean fewer laser on/off switches. The drawing is a sketch with five pieces; in the demo every wall already arrives as one straight line.

lines: // Connect polylines to longer polylines and reduce the number of points.
// All distances in mm: end points closer than 0.001 mm (1 micrometer)
// are treated as the same point. Self connect: a polyline whose start
// and end meet is closed. Point reduction removes points that deviate
// less than 0.001 mm from a straight line; the negative edge length
// limit (-1) means that no edges are removed because of their length.
// Reduce the number of direction changes.
// Segments within 0.02 mm of one straight line count as collinear and
// go into the same block, also across gaps of up to 4 mm (the laser
// skips the gap). bFlipLines: segments that point the other way are
// flipped, so the whole line is exposed in one direction.
// Reduce the jump length (blocks may be flipped).
// The first block is the one near the platform origin (0, 0); then the
// next block is chosen to keep the jumps short.
// The model subtype marks the vectors as support (not part), e.g. for
// the preview, the sorting and the export.

steps.title: Laser settings and order
notes: Wall supports (BSID 700) run at 180 W and 1000 mm/s. Scan order 10 makes them the very first vectors of a layer, before solid supports (20) and the part.

recipes.title: Wall supports on every second layer by default
recipes.why: Supports are removed after the build; exposing them on every second layer saves time.
recipes.result: New profiles expose the walls on every second layer, as in the video. Set Expose every n-th layer to 2 in the Layer skip view.

recipes.title: Do not bridge gaps in a wall
recipes.why: Each separate wall piece should be its own block, for example to inspect the sliced data.
recipes.result: Collinear lines are still merged where they touch, but pieces with a gap stay separate blocks: the Clean-up view would end with three blocks instead of one.

recipes.title: More power for the walls
recipes.why: With layer skip the exposure melts two powder layers at once and may need more energy.
recipes.result: Wall support default 220 W. For one profile, change Scanning › Wall support › power in the dialog instead.
